subject: paediatrics
title: Mucopolysaccharidoses, Skeletal Dysostosis and Organic Acidaemias

steps.tx: Progressive connective tissue and visceral deposition of glycosaminoglycans produces recognizable multi-system deformities. Defective lysosomal degradation of dermatan sulfate, heparan sulfate, or keratan sulfate produces **mucopolysaccharidosis disorders**, characterized by progressive coarsening of facial features, cognitive impairment, hepatosplenomegaly, and stiff contracted joints. Clinical phenotypes range from severe infant-onset neurodegenerative syndromes to attenuated adult-onset forms with preserved intelligence.
steps.say: Mucopolysaccharidoses result from defective degradation of glycosaminoglycans. Patients develop coarse facial features, intellectual decline, hepatosplenomegaly, and stiff joints.

vis.alt: Biochemical degradation of glycosaminoglycans and resulting organ pathology in mucopolysaccharidoses.
vis.caption: Glycosaminoglycan accumulation pathways, dysostosis multiplex, and organ pathology in mucopolysaccharidoses. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Severe alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency creates the classic gargoyle clinical phenotype. The prototypical severe form, **Hurler syndrome MPS I**, is transmitted as an autosomal recessive trait on chromosome 4p16, resulting in progressive accumulation of dermatan and heparan sulfate. Affected infants appear normal at birth but develop coarse facial features, depressed nasal bridge, thick lips, macroglossia, corneal clouding, claw hand deformities, and severe neurocognitive decline by two years.
steps.say: Hurler syndrome is an autosomal recessive alpha-L-iduronidase defect storing dermatan and heparan sulfate. Features include coarse facies, corneal clouding, claw hands, and neurodevelopmental decline.

steps.tx: X-linked inheritance and clear corneas distinguish the second major mucopolysaccharide storage disorder. Transmitted as the only X-linked recessive form among the mucopolysaccharidoses, **Hunter syndrome MPS II** results from iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency. Affected boys present with coarse facial features, short stature, joint stiffness, and pebbly ivory-coloured skin papules over the scapulae, but characteristically maintain completely clear corneas without clouding.
steps.say: Hunter syndrome is the only X-linked mucopolysaccharidosis, caused by iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency. Boys develop coarse features and joint stiffness but characteristically maintain clear corneas.

rows: Pebbly skin lesion unique to Hunter

steps.tx: Storage material thickens bone unevenly and deforms the growing spine. On this lateral film the upper lumbar vertebrae show **anterior inferior beaking**, where the front lower corner juts forward like a small hook, tilting the spine into a sharp gibbus at the thoracolumbar junction. That beaked vertebra is a classic skeletal signature of Hurler syndrome within the wider pattern of dysostosis multiplex.
steps.say: Hurler syndrome beaks the front lower corner of L1 and L2, tilting the spine into a gibbus. That hooked vertebra is a classic part of dysostosis multiplex.

vis.alt: Side view radiograph of the lower spine showing wedge shaped upper lumbar vertebrae with beak like projections and a sharp kyphotic bend.
vis.caption: Lateral thoracolumbar radiograph in Hurler syndrome showing anterior inferior beaking of L1 and L2 with a kyphotic gibbus. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Generalized skeletal involvement produces pathognomonic radiographical alterations across the axial and appendicular skeleton. Radiographs reveal generalized **dysostosis multiplex skeletal changes**, featuring an enlarged J-shaped sella turcica, oar-shaped or spatulate widening of the ribs, anterior inferior beaking of the lumbar vertebral bodies at L1 and L2 causing thoracic gibbus, and hypoplastic pelvic acetabula with flared iliac wings and tapered metacarpal bases.
steps.say: Dysostosis multiplex features an enlarged J-shaped sella turcica, spatulate ribs, lumbar vertebral beaking causing kyphosis, and tapered metacarpal bones on plain radiographs.

rows: Anterior beaking of L1 and L2

steps.tx: Defective keratan sulfate degradation provokes severe dwarfism without cognitive compromise. In **Morquio syndrome MPS IV**, deficiency of N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfate sulfatase impairs keratan sulfate catabolism, producing severe short-trunk dwarfism, pectus carinatum, and corneal clouding, while cognitive development remains entirely normal. Odontoid hypoplasia represents a life-threatening complication, risking fatal atlantoaxial subluxation and cervical cord compression upon minor neck flexion.
steps.say: Morquio syndrome causes severe short-trunk dwarfism and odontoid hypoplasia with preserved intelligence. Odontoid hypoplasia risks fatal cervical cord compression during minor neck trauma.

steps.tx: Enzymatic defects in branched-chain amino acid and odd-chain fatty acid oxidation produce acute toxic decompensations. The disorders termed **organic acidaemias** encompass methylmalonic acidaemia, propionic acidaemia, and isovaleric acidaemia, caused by inherited blocks in intermediary catabolism. Neonates appear healthy for twenty-four to forty-eight hours until protein feeding triggers sudden refusal, vomiting, lethargy, hypothermia, progressive coma, and severe high anion gap metabolic acidosis.
steps.say: Organic acidaemias block branched-chain amino acid oxidation. Protein ingestion triggers sudden metabolic acidosis, vomiting, lethargy, high anion gap, and ketonuria within days of birth.

steps.tx: Laboratory evaluation discriminates organic acidaemias from primary urea cycle and respiratory pathologies. Key biochemical findings in organic acidaemias include **high anion gap metabolic acidosis**, marked ketonuria, moderate hyperammonaemia, and profound bone marrow suppression with neutropenia and thrombocytopenia. In contrast, urea cycle disorders present with central respiratory alkalosis, absence of significant metabolic acidosis, and negative urinary ketones despite massive hyperammonaemia.
steps.say: Organic acidaemias present with high anion gap metabolic acidosis, heavy ketonuria, and neutropenia. In contrast, urea cycle defects show respiratory alkalosis without ketonuria.

right.title: Urea Cycle Disorder Profile
points: Normal white blood cells and platelets

steps.tx: Emergency stabilization requires immediate cessation of protein intake and aggressive caloric replenishment. Acute metabolic management demands stopping all dietary protein, infusing ten percent dextrose with intravenous carnitine to promote toxic acylcarnitine excretion, and administering cofactor trials with **intravenous hydroxocobalamin** in methylmalonic acidaemia or biotin in propionic acidaemia. Emergency hemodialysis or continuous filtration is initiated promptly if severe intractable acidosis or hyperammonaemia persists.
steps.say: Managing organic acidaemia crises requires stopping protein feeds, infusing intravenous dextrose and carnitine, and testing vitamin B12 or biotin cofactors before hemodialysis.
